about_preview.label: About
about_preview.title: Greg Mittelette
about_preview.quote_translation: We don't learn for school, but for life.
about_preview.text: Over 1,100 students mentored. 80% admitted to a top 30 global university or grande ecole. Our edge: we know the final destination (Stanford, Polytechnique, EPFL), which lets us build the right path from day one.

q1.question: What commitment does this require from the family?
q1.answer: Serious mentoring is teamwork. We expect consistency in sessions, transparency on transcripts and goals, and real parent involvement in orientation decisions. In return, we commit to personalized follow-up and genuine availability between sessions.

q2.question: When should we start?
q2.answer: The earlier, the better. Ideally 6th-7th grade: we build the math foundations, choose the right curriculum, anticipate the key transitions. But we also work with students who come in during 11th or 12th grade : the work is different, more intensive, but the results are there.

q3.question: How many students do you take on?
q3.answer: Few. We follow each student personally, sometimes over several years. It's not a scalable model and that's by design. If we're full, we'll tell you : we'd rather say no than do it halfway.

q4.question: What does the process look like?
q4.answer: We start with a diagnostic: current level, ambitions, target schools. From there we propose a work plan. Sessions are weekly, in person or via video. We check in regularly with parents and adjust based on results and deadlines.

q5.question: Do you work with families abroad?
q5.answer: Most of our clients are expats or between two countries. We work via video with families in Dubai, Singapore, London, New York. French system, AEFE schools, IB, BFI : we know these curricula and more importantly, how they translate in admissions files.

tutoring.hero_subtitle: Private mathematics and physics-chemistry lessons over video, from middle school to the gates of the prépas. Fourteen years of teaching, one method: find where the marks are lost, then take them back one by one.
tutoring.method_text1: A lesson with me is not going over the textbook again. It is understanding where the student loses marks, why, and closing the gap between their actual level and what their school, and their ambitions, demand.
tutoring.method_text2: I teach these curricula from the inside: the French maths specialism, maths expertes, bilingual and international tracks : EJM, Saint-Germain, Franklin, École Alsacienne. tutoring.method_text3: Every session aims at something measurable: the average that recovers, the distinction, the file that opens EPFL, Polytechnique or an elite prépa.
tutoring.subject_math_desc: From middle school to maths expertes and ahead into the prépa syllabus. Proofs, analysis, algebra : the French curriculum taught to the standard of the best lycées.

about.title: The Founder
about.subtitle: "Non scholae, sed vitae discimus" – Seneca
about.bio_text1: Centrale Lyon for engineering, ISTIA for organization, MIT X for supply chain analytics. I saw from the inside how admissions actually work. Who gets in, who doesn't, and why.
about.bio_text2: The most invested families are often the most misguided. They pay for tutoring, stack extracurriculars, hope the grades will speak for themselves. Meanwhile, the spots go to those who understood the rules of the game.
about.bio_text3: For 14 years, I've been bridging those two worlds. From 6th grade to the gates of Stanford, Polytechnique, EPFL. By building a strategy: which curriculum, which timeline, which positioning, so that on decision day, the application leaves no doubt.
about.bio_text4: 1,100 students. The reality hasn't changed: when you know where you're going, every decision becomes obvious.
about.philosophy_text1: I take on few students. That's a choice. Because my job is to know each one of them : their transcripts, their strengths, what they hide, what holds them back.
about.philosophy_text2: I follow them over the long run. Sometimes from 6th grade to the moment they open the letter. When I build an application for Stanford, Oxford or Ginette, I'm not taking a guess : I know what separates a yes from a no.
about.philosophy_text3: I live internationally, like most of my clients. We understand each other because we share the same reality: an ambition for our children, opaque systems, and the refusal to leave it to chance.
about.philosophy_text4: Today, I'm preparing my own children, aged 9 and 11, exactly the way I prepare my students. Same rigor, same vision. That's the most honest proof of what I believe in.

schools.intro_text: A university admission is prepared years in advance, and it often starts with the choice of a school. For years we have been working with pupils from Jeannine Manuel, Franklin, École alsacienne and the Lycée international de Saint-Germain: we know what these schools expect, and what really counts at entry.

schools.step3_desc: A review of every school report, preparation for the assessment and interview in the months before the deadline, an application reviewed, and the right moment to apply.
schools.rule1: No place is ever promised: we prepare your child, the school decides.
schools.rule2: Two well-chosen schools are worth more than four random applications.

tomorrow.meta_title: What future for our children with AI? An action plan | Carmine Admission
tomorrow.meta_description: Is a prépa still worth it? Should they learn to code? Does maths still matter? An action plan for your child, built on their profile, by Greg Mittelette.
tomorrow.label: Tomorrow's world
tomorrow.hero_title: What future for our children with AI?
tomorrow.hero_subtitle: The parents who write to me all ask the same question in different words: will what my child learns today still be worth anything in ten years? The answer exists, but it is different for every child: I build it with you, as an action plan.
tomorrow.scene_text: One evening at dinner, your fourteen-year-old daughter puts down her phone and asks: "What's the point of learning all this, if AI already does it?" You have an answer. You're not sure it will hold for ten years.
tomorrow.scene_after: That question deserves more than an opinion. It deserves a plan.
tomorrow.q1_title: Is a prépa still worth it?
tomorrow.q1_desc: The answer depends less on AI than on the child: what they aim for, what they enjoy working on, what they can sustain. For some it is still the best springboard; for others, a costly detour. (A prépa is France's two-year selective track into the top engineering and business schools.)
tomorrow.q2_desc: Writing code line by line matters less than it used to. Knowing what you want to build, and checking what the machine produces, matters more.
tomorrow.q3_desc: Maths is what lets you judge what AI claims. And it remains the subject that opens or closes the most selective tracks.
tomorrow.q4_title: Which degrees will still hold up in ten years?
tomorrow.q4_desc: Nobody knows the list of jobs in 2036. What you can do is choose studies that keep several doors open, and avoid those that leave only one.
tomorrow.vision_title: AI doesn't replace a direction. It makes it matter more.
tomorrow.v1_text: When a machine can summarise, translate and calculate, value moves to what it does poorly: reasoning soundly, choosing, building something that didn't exist. This is built early, and it shows in an application.
tomorrow.v2_text: Selective universities are not disappearing with AI; what they look for is changing. A student who has led a real project, taken on hard problems and can explain what they understood stays a step ahead.
tomorrow.v3_text: Not one subject among others: a trajectory that starts in middle school and decides what is still open when the time comes to choose.
tomorrow.example_title: An action plan, on one page you can come back to
tomorrow.example_intro: This is what the summary of a plan looks like. The student is fictional; the format is the one families receive.
tomorrow.doc_student: Léa, 14, in Year 10 at the French lycée in Singapore
tomorrow.doc_profile: Quick with numbers, bored in class. Loves drawing and building games. A move back to Europe is planned in two years.
tomorrow.doc_target: An engineering school with a design dimension, in Switzerland or France.
tomorrow.doc_alt: An international bachelor's in product design. A science prépa, if her taste for abstraction is confirmed.
tomorrow.doc_t1: Rework 3D geometry. First junior maths competition. One project: model and 3D-print an object, documenting every step.
tomorrow.doc_t2: Next year's course choices aligned with the path. Certified English. One week of job shadowing in a design office.
tomorrow.doc_t3: The subjects and options the target schools require. A personal project to show. The application calendar set.
tomorrow.about_text1: I have taught mathematics for fourteen years, to more than 1,100 students, and I guide applications to the most selective universities.
tomorrow.about_text2: I work with AI every day. I have built with it the tools my students use: Fields for olympiad problems, Summit for the SAT, Xiaomo for Chinese. I don't talk about AI from a distance.
tomorrow.step1_desc: The child, the family, the setting. Questionnaires, a maths test, a conversation with you, then with them alone.
tomorrow.step2_desc: The path to aim for, and one or two realistic alternatives. What opens them, what closes them.
tomorrow.step3_desc: The written document, then a video call to go through it together.
tomorrow.step4_title: We review it at six months
tomorrow.step4_desc: Optional: we check the plan still holds, and adjust it.

adults.meta_title: AI scares me: an action plan for you | Carmine Admission
adults.meta_description: Will your job change? Should you learn AI, and what exactly? An action plan built on your situation, by Greg Mittelette.
adults.label: For you
adults.hero_title: AI scares me: where do I start?
adults.hero_subtitle: You worry about your children, and sometimes about yourself: your job, your place, what you ought to learn. I offer parents what I do for their children: look at the situation squarely, and come out with an action plan.
adults.questions_title: Four questions that keep coming back
adults.q1_desc: Rarely all at once. It is tasks that change. Knowing which ones, in your own work, changes the question entirely.
adults.q2_title: Should I learn AI, and what exactly?
adults.q2_desc: Not everything. What serves your work and your plans. A general course is reassuring; targeted learning saves time from the first week.
adults.q3_title: Is it too late to change?
adults.q3_desc: The tools are quick to learn when you start from your own work. What matters is the order in which you take them on.
adults.q4_desc: With an honest inventory: what you do, what AI can already do, what it won't. The rest follows.
adults.vision_title: Fear comes from what we don't look at squarely.
adults.vision_text1: AI doesn't hit everyone the same way. Within the same job, some tasks become faster and others gain value. Most people have never sorted this out for their own work.
adults.vision_text2: Learning AI from your own job is much faster than a general course. That is what I did: as a teacher, I built with it the tools my students use today.
adults.vision_text3: And what you learn also helps your children. A parent who understands AI guides their choices better.
adults.proof_title: I work with AI every day
adults.proof_text1: I have taught mathematics for fourteen years, to more than 1,100 students, and I guide applications to the most selective universities.
adults.proof_text2: I built with AI the tools my students use: Fields, for olympiad problems; Summit, for the SAT; Xiaomo, for Chinese. I won't talk to you about AI from a distance.
adults.step1_desc: Your job, your actual tasks, your skills, your constraints, what you want. A questionnaire, then a conversation.
adults.step2_desc: What AI changes in your work: what is exposed, what gains value, what it won't do.
adults.step3_desc: A written document: what to learn, in what order, which tools to adopt, with which deadlines. Then a video call to go through it together.
adults.step4_title: We review it at three months
adults.step4_desc: Optional: we check what has been put in place, and adjust.
